title: RAINS : RAPTURES AND RAVAGES
author: Soubhagyabanta Moharana/ସୌଭାଗ୍ୟବନ୍ତ ମହାରଣା
text:
Sometimes droplets of poetic emotions
Penetrate the hard granite
To transform the rock into a soft flower.
Rains are like tears of dark clouds
Expressing intensity of joys
To celebrate primordial tranquillity
Amidst heat and dust of parched soil.

The dry earth unbearably
Becomes hungry and destitute
Like drought-affected emaciated people
Due to dearth of waters.
Rains come as boons of ambrosia
To create heart-throbs
In the decaying and dying earth.

Rainbow is like a necklace of colours,
A marvellous metaphor
Embracing the cloudy sky
To coax the angels of rim-jhim rains
For scintillating welcome
To rejuvenate the inanimate sky.

Yet the rainy season being rapturous
Enchants the earth like a magic
For an uncanny metamorphosis
To smile upon its pastoral beauties
And bounties of pervading nature.

Rains are sometimes raptures
Of sweet dreams and sensualities
Sometimes melting agonies
Of broken hearts and despairs of marooned victims
Due to ravages by heavy floods and cloud-bursts
To measure the abysmal depth of depression
And unstinted spirit of exhilaration.
